result.topic: Adversarial verification of the Rust agent's findings: nokhwa 0.10.11 MSMF, rawusb 0.1.7, libusb, nusb, and compile checks (Windows 11, host Gerald)

verdicts.claim: 1. nokhwa 0.10.11 (MSMF) passes native MJPEG bytes through unchanged at 1280x720@30 (C922 593/593 at 30.02 fps, 144 KB; C930e 589/589 at 30.06 fps, 85 KB; Kiyo 424/424 at 30.03 fps, 107 KB) and reports the format as '1280x720@1 MJPEG'.
verdicts.reason: The cited files match: 20261025T183903Z_camsall_1280x720/analysis.json gives C922 593 valid, 30.021 fps, p50 144016 B and C930e 589 valid, 30.065 fps, p50 85306 B; 20261025T180337Z_cams5 gives Kiyo 424 valid, 30.029 fps, p50 106879 B. My re-runs reproduce this for the C922, C930e and the generic 4C4A:4A55. To check that the bytes come from the camera, I compared JPEG header segments with a script. nokhwa frames from the C922 and C930e have the same DQT, DHT, SOF0, COM, APP0 and DRI digests as MF-native (converters disabled) frames and as earlier PyAV-dshow passthrough frames. That layout is Logitech's own: DQT comes before SOF, and COM and APP0 are zero-filled. A re-encoder would write its own JFIF header. The 4C4A changes its quantisation tables over the first frames, and nokhwa's frames 0, 1 and 2 have exactly the same DQT digests as MF-native frames 0, 1 and 2 (1ba2be6b89, 48355af8db, 5e414b2ffa). The Kiyo frame from 18:03Z has the same APP0, SOF0 and DHT as Kiyo frames from gst-mfvideosrc and MF. Only its DQT and APP15 quality byte differ, and that frame was warm-up frame 0. The '@1' comes from a bug in nokhwa-bindings-windows-0.4.6/src/lib.rs lines 952-953: `fps as u32` keeps only the denominator of the packed MFRatio. Caveats: (a) The Kiyo could not be re-tested. Since about 19:04Z it fails with 0x8007001F in nokhwa and in the MF reference tool, while DevNodeStatus stays 0x180200A (no DN_NEED_RESTART). (b) With all four cameras open at once, the Kiyo failed and the C930e failed with 0x800718CF (not enough bandwidth). The C930e shares hub 13.1 with the 4C4A. (c) nokhwa's set_format (lib.rs around line 1047) matches the requested fps against MF_MT_FRAME_RATE_RANGE_MAX and RANGE_MIN as well as FRAME_RATE, so it can pick the wrong type. A 60 fps request delivered 29.7 fps. The test is inconclusive, though: the MF reference tool with the native type explicitly set to 15/1 or 60/1 also delivered about 30 fps from the C922. No harness currently proves the negotiated frame rate. (d) The 4C4A ran at only 25.77 fps when asked for 30.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: Commands: camlock -> nokhwa_probe.exe capture --cameras match:<vidpid> --width 1280 --height 720 --fps 30 --seconds 15 --exposure -7 --wb 4000 --decode-every 30 --save-samples 2 --out <S>\single_* (wrapper script scratchpad\verify_tools\seq_single.sh). Results: C922 442/442 SOI+EOI, 15/15 decoded, 29.97 fps, median 141169 B. C930e 438/438, 30.03 fps, 131919 B. 4C4A 386/386, 25.77 fps, 40375 B. Kiyo 0 frames, 0x8007001F. All four at once (19:04Z, <S>\cap_all4): C922 593/593, 30.00 fps; 4C4A 513/513, 25.77 fps; Kiyo 0x8007001F; C930e 0x800718CF. MF reference: camlock -> mjpeg/build/mf_mjpeg_capture.exe --dev <vidpid> --fps 30 ... (scratchpad\verify_tools\seq_mf.sh). Header check: python scratchpad\verify_tools\jpeghdr.py label=path ...

verdicts.claim: 2. On Windows, nokhwa's Buffer::capture_timestamp is the MF IMFSample time (QPC, 100 ns units) plus a per-stream epoch, not Unix time. With the epoch removed it is on the host QPC clock. Median host_arrival minus sample_time: C922 16.2 ms, C930e 0.41 ms, Kiyo 32.4 ms.
verdicts.reason: The epoch arithmetic is correct. In nokhwa-bindings-windows-0.4.6/src/lib.rs, lines 1134-1135 set stream_epoch = SystemTime::now() since UNIX_EPOCH inside start_stream. Lines 1179-1184 return epoch + llTimestamp*100 ns, and only when llTimestamp > 0. The doc comment at line 415 says sample times are 'relative to stream start', which is wrong: the observed llTimestamp is about 102,911 s, the same as QPC uptime, so the result is a wall-clock value plus QPC uptime and is meaningless as-is. The probe removes the epoch using the midpoint of a roughly 10 µs bracket around open_stream. The MF reference tool, which reads llTimestamp directly, gives the same latency distributions: C922 16.24 ms, C930e 0.33 ms, 4C4A 32.30 ms, against nokhwa's 16.25-16.36, 0.39 and 32.36. So nokhwa adds nothing. However, the medians are artifacts and do not describe the cameras. On every camera, every backend and every run, sample times fall on a 16 ms grid: intervals are only 32 or 48 ms, and each stream keeps a fixed phase modulo 16 ms (for example 7.4 ms for the C922 and 5.4 ms for the 4C4A in the same run). Latency is multimodal at {0, 16, 32} ms, and the median just reflects the mix of modes. The C922 gave a median of 0.38 ms in one run (when 60 fps was requested), and the C930e has about 33% of frames in the 16 ms mode. The metadata registry value is not what causes this: the 4C4A has no MetadataBufferSizeInKB0 and has_capture_metadata=False, yet shows the same 16 ms grid. Removing the value on the C922 needs elevation, so that is untested. The Kiyo's 32.4 ms is not in its analysis.json, whose latency field is about -1.0e8 ms because of an old age-method bug. It can only be recomputed from implied_sample_time_ns, which gives a median of 32.36 ms. Conclusion: MF sample time is QPC-domain but quantised to 16 ms on this host. It is not a measure of when light hit the sensor. The MF tool shows 32-byte UVC payload headers present for the C922 and C930e (has_capture_metadata=True), which is the better route for timing.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: nokhwa single, 30 fps request: C922 median 16.36 ms (hist 0-1 ms: 183, 16-17 ms: 225); C930e median 0.39 (0 ms: 246, 16 ms: 125+11); 4C4A median 32.36 (16 ms: 25, 32 ms: 331). C922 with 15 fps request: 16.43. C922 with 60 fps request: 0.38. MF reference: C922 16.24, C930e 0.33, 4C4A 32.30. Sample-time intervals were always {32, 48} ms. Analysis: python scratchpad\verify_tools\an.py <run_dir>

verdicts.claim: 3. MF exposes NV12 alongside MJPEG with identical counts even with converters disabled (C922 120 MJPG / 120 NV12 / 98 YUY2), and nokhwa's format list drops some native types.
verdicts.reason: rust_mf_native_types/1792951371/summary.json shows C922 MJPG 120, NV12 120, YUY2 98; C930e 119/119/97; Kiyo H264 56, MJPG 28, NV12 28, YUY2 28. The converters-enabled reader failed with 0xC00D3E85, so no enabled-vs-disabled comparison was actually made. Extra context from the libusb descriptors: the C922 has only YUY2 and MJPEG UVC formats, so MF's NV12 types are synthesised. The Kiyo has a native UNCOMPRESSED:NV12 format. The drop is worse than claimed. nokhwa's public compatible_camera_formats() returns at most 2 fourccs (nokhwa-0.10.11/src/backends/capture/msmf_backend.rs lines 163-178), so MJPEG never appears for the C922 or C930e (my re-run lists only NV12 309 and YUYV 240). guid_to_frameformat drops H264, non-integer rates such as 7.5 fps are zeroed, and entries are triplicated. Capture still works because MediaFoundationCaptureDevice::new uses the internal full list.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: camlock -> nokhwa_probe.exe list --out <S>\list: C922 549 entries {NV12 309, YUYV 240}; 4C4A 60 {NV12 30, MJPEG 30}; Kiyo 168 {YUYV 84, MJPEG 84}; C930e 549 {NV12 306, YUYV 243}.

verdicts.claim: 4. rawusb 0.1.7 on Windows enumerates only the two Intel root hubs and never sees usbvideo-bound cameras.
verdicts.reason: The cited rust_uvc_iso_list_rawusb/1792953547/summary.json and my re-run both list only 8086:7a60 and 8086:1138, each with raw_config_error 'no such configuration: entity not found', and zero UVC devices. rawusb's Windows backend is WinUSB-based (src/sys/windows/ffi.rs).
verdicts.rerun_numbers: camlock -> uvc_iso.exe list --backend rawusb --out <S>\rawusb_list: uvc_devices 0, non_uvc 2 (Intel root hubs).

verdicts.claim: 5. The libusb backend on Windows enumerates all devices and reads UVC descriptors without opening the camera (Kiyo alt1 3072 B, alt2 33792 B; C922 11 alts 192..3060 B per microframe, dwClockFrequency 30 MHz, UVC 1.00; 4C4A one alt 3069 B). The C930e config descriptor read fails with LIBUSB_ERROR_NOT_FOUND because of the Logitech composite INF oem74.inf.
verdicts.reason: Enumeration and the alt-setting sizes reproduce, and the list path never calls libusb_open (backend_libusb.rs: libusb_open only in open()). Two parts are wrong. (1) The C922's dwClockFrequency is 300,000,000 Hz (300 MHz), not 30 MHz. This is in the agent's own file (rust_uvc_iso_list_libusb/1792953547/summary.json line 616), in my re-run, and in py_libusb1_list/result.json. The Kiyo and 4C4A are 30 MHz. (2) The C930e descriptor is readable without opening the device. Only libusb_get_active_config_descriptor fails (-5, NOT_FOUND). libusb_get_config_descriptor(dev, 0) returns all 2573 bytes, tested with libusb 1.0.29. python-libusb1 also read the C930e descriptors at 18:21Z and 18:46Z with the same INF. The parent device does use oem74.inf (provider Logitech, service usbccgp, versus Microsoft usb.inf for the C922 and 4C4A), so the INF may be why the active configuration cannot be found. That cause is untested. The failure is in the harness's choice of API, not a hard limit.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: camlock -> uvc_iso.exe list --backend libusb --out <S>\libusb_list: 1532:0e05 Super 4.4 alts [(1,3072),(2,33792)] 30 MHz; 046d:085c High port 1, 11 alts 192..3060, 300 MHz, UVC 1.00; 4c4a:4a55 High 13.1.3, alt (1,3069), 30 MHz; 046d:0843 LIBUSB_ERROR_NOT_FOUND. A/B test: uv run --script scratchpad\verify_tools\cfgdesc_ab.py gives C930e active_rc -5 and index0_rc 0 with wTotalLength 2573; the other three cameras pass both calls.

verdicts.claim: 6. Neither backend can stream while usbvideo owns the cameras.
verdicts.reason: The cited stream summaries show libusb failing with 'libusb_open: LIBUSB_ERROR_NOT_FOUND' at stage 'open', and rawusb failing with 'device ... not found', for both the Kiyo and the C922. I did not re-run this. The C930e and 4C4A were never tested, though rawusb cannot see them and libusb has no driver for usbvideo-bound interfaces.

verdicts.claim: 7. Compile status: uvc_iso (rawusb) builds and cross-checks for Linux and macOS; uvc_iso+libusb builds on the host; nokhwa_probe cross-checks fail in v4l2-sys/objc build scripts; nusb has no Isochronous transfer type (E0425); the 'uvc' crate fails on mozjpeg-sys; the 'libuvc' crate fails in libuvc-sys.
verdicts.reason: The nusb part is confirmed by my re-run and by the source. cargo check of cc_nusb_iso_fail fails with E0425 'cannot find type Isochronous in module nusb::transfer' on the host, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and aarch64-apple-darwin, and cc_nusb_bulk_ok passes. In nusb 0.2.9 (latest on crates.io, GitHub release v0.2.9 on 2026-10-24), EndpointType is implemented only for Bulk and Interrupt, and that is also true of src/transfer/mod.rs on main today. There are no unreleased iso branches (branches: add_illumos, android, main, v0.1, v0.1-winusb-associated-interface). PR #178 (Linux-only iso) is open but stalled; its author stepped away on 2026-06-30. PR #233 (cross-platform iso) was closed unmerged on 2026-09-18. Issue #47 is still open. On 2026-09-21 the maintainer said UVC class support is out of scope and recommended kernel UVC drivers. nusb Bulk could in principle serve a bulk-endpoint UVC camera, but all four cameras here are isochronous. Corrections to the other parts, from the files: the 'uvc' crate fails at dependency resolution because every mozjpeg-sys 0.10.x release is yanked, not during a build. All cross-target failures (libusb1-sys, v4l2-sys-mit, objc_exception, camera-rs) come from missing cross C toolchains (e.g. 'failed to find tool x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc'), so they say nothing about whether the code ports. The cross-target rows are cargo check only, with no linking.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: cd research/usb_cameras/rust/compile_checks/cc_nusb_iso_fail && cargo check --release --locked [--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu|aarch64-apple-darwin] --target-dir <S>\cargo_target exits 101 with E0425 on all three targets; cc_nusb_bulk_ok exits 0. rustc 1.99.1. gh api repos/kevinmehall/nusb/{releases,branches,issues/178,issues/233,issues/47}.

verdicts.reason: bash -n passes for rust/platform/run_linux.sh, run_macos.sh, run_windows_phase2.sh and rust/run_windows_nokhwa.sh. They have not been run on Linux or macOS; the scripts label themselves 'unverified'.

harness_bugs: nokhwa_probe build used for 20261025T180337Z: os_timestamp_ns came from the wrong age-method mapping (201550317078400 is about 2x QPC). As a result latency_host_minus_os_ms in that run's analysis.json is about -1.0077e8 ms. The Kiyo's 32.4 ms figure can only be recovered from implied_sample_time_ns. The stale analysis.json is still in results.

nokhwa_probe capture loop retries errors with no backoff, giving 13-17 million read_errors in 15-20 s when a camera fails (Kiyo 0x8007001F, C930e 0x800718CF). It burns a core and makes read_errors meaningless.

nokhwa_probe takes 'actual_format' fps from nokhwa's broken field ('@1'). It never reads MF_MT_FRAME_RATE or the sample duration itself, so the negotiated rate is never verified. The C922 delivered about 30 fps for 15 and 60 fps requests.
nokhwa_probe --save-samples saves frames from seq 0 (warm-up). On the 4C4A and Kiyo these have different DQT/APP15 from steady state, which can make header comparisons look like a mismatch.
run_windows_nokhwa.sh omits the generic 4C4A:4A55 camera and writes into the repo results tree by default.
uvc_iso: unknown flags such as --help silently run 'list' and write a result into research/usb_cameras/results (I hit this; the accidental output was moved to <S>\rawusb_list_accidental_help).
uvc_iso libusb backend only calls libusb_get_active_config_descriptor, so the C930e reads as a failure even though libusb_get_config_descriptor(dev, 0) works. It should fall back to index 0.
uvc_iso reports iso_alt_bandwidth.approx_fraction_of_hs_periodic_budget for SuperSpeed devices too (Kiyo alt2 = 5.632), which is meaningless.

uvc_iso backend_libusb rebuild_raw writes every endpoint descriptor as 7 bytes, but audio endpoints are 9 bytes. raw_config_len is therefore short of wTotalLength (Kiyo 1452 vs 1460, C922 2497 vs 2503, 4C4A 650 vs 652) and is not the raw descriptor.
drafted_test_issues: Claim 2 reports medians of a multimodal {0, 16, 32} ms distribution. The harness should report how many frames fall in each mode and the sample-time phase modulo 16 ms instead. Running the C922 with and without MetadataBufferSizeInKB0 needs elevation, so the metadata question is untested for the C922. The 4C4A (no metadata) shows the same 16 ms grid.

No test proves the frame rate nokhwa negotiates. The C922 delivered 30 fps even when the MF reference tool set the native type to 15/1 or 60/1 (sample_duration 666666). The fps question needs a camera that honours rate changes, or a check of the device's UVC commit (PROBE/COMMIT) state.

Kiyo streaming is currently broken in nokhwa and the MF reference tool (0x8007001F, 19:04-19:07Z), while DevNodeStatus is 0x180200A with no DN_NEED_RESTART (checked again at 19:26Z). Kiyo results from 18:03Z cannot be reproduced right now. Evidence: <S>\single_vid_1532_pid_0e05_30\summary.json and <S>\mf_kiyo_30\meta.json.
With all four cameras open at once, the C930e fails with 0x800718CF because it shares hub 13.1 (ports 3 and 4) with the 4C4A. Multi-camera claims should state which cameras share a hub.
Claim 6 was only tested on the Kiyo and C922; the C930e and 4C4A were not tested.
The MF native-types test never got a converters-enabled reader (0xC00D3E85), so 'even with converters disabled' has no enabled baseline to compare against.
result.corrected_summary:
The core findings hold. Claims 3, 4, 6 and 7 and the script parse check are confirmed; claims 1 and 2 are confirmed with significant caveats and claim 5 needs two corrections.

**Native MJPEG through nokhwa (claim 1).** nokhwa 0.10.11 on MSMF passes the camera's own MJPEG bytes through unchanged. JPEG header segments match MF-native and DirectShow passthrough frames for the C922, C930e and 4C4A, and the 4C4A's quantisation-table ramp over the first frames matches frame for frame. The C922 and C930e produce identical JPEG headers apart from the restart interval (DRI), which fits your remark that the C930e is almost the same camera. Two things are broken in nokhwa:
- **Frame rate field:** it reports '@1' because it truncates the packed frame-rate ratio.
- **Format list:** its public format list returns at most two fourccs, so MJPEG is missing for the C922 and C930e, and H264 and 7.5 fps modes are dropped.

**Timestamps (claim 2).** The capture timestamp is the MF sample time plus a wall-clock value taken at stream start. Removing that value gives QPC-domain times, and the MF reference tool gives the same numbers. But on this host, sample times sit on a 16 ms grid for all cameras, and the delay from sample time to arrival falls into 0, 16 or 32 ms modes. That makes the per-camera medians (C922 16 ms, C930e 0.4 ms, Kiyo and 4C4A 32 ms) artifacts of the mode mix, not camera properties: one C922 run gave a median of 0.38 ms. The metadata registry setting does not cause the grid, since the 4C4A, which lacks it, shows it too. MF sample time is therefore not an accurate time for when light hit the sensor. The UVC payload headers that MF exposes on the C922 and C930e are the better source.

**rawusb (claim 4).** rawusb 0.1.7 sees only the two Intel root hubs.

**libusb descriptors (claim 5).** libusb reads descriptors without opening any camera, but two details were wrong:
- The C922's clock frequency is 300 MHz, not 30 MHz.
- The C930e descriptor is readable. Only the 'active config' call fails; reading config index 0 returns all 2573 bytes. The Logitech INF (oem74.inf) is confirmed on the parent device, but whether it causes the failure is untested.

**Streaming (claim 6).** Neither backend can stream while usbvideo owns the cameras. This was tested on the Kiyo and C922 only.

**Compile status (claim 7).** nusb 0.2.9, the latest release and also current main, has no isochronous endpoint type; I reproduced the E0425 error on all three targets. The only isochronous PRs are #178 (Linux-only, stalled) and #233 (closed unmerged). The 'uvc' crate fails because every mozjpeg-sys 0.10.x release is yanked, not during a build. The cross-target failures come from missing cross C toolchains, not from the code.

**Scripts.** All four drafted scripts pass `bash -n`; none has been run on Linux or macOS.

**Kiyo.** The Kiyo was not re-tested. Since 19:04Z it fails to stream in both nokhwa and the MF reference tool (0x8007001F), while its DevNodeStatus stays 0x180200A with no DN_NEED_RESTART.

**Stray file.** Passing `--help` to uvc_iso ran a rawusb list and wrote a result into the repo, because unknown flags fall through to `list` (harness bug). I moved that output to `C:\Users\Dom\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-Dom-GitHub-freemocap-skellycam\96d4d83a-4013-4e95-a9bd-1cfedc6522c8\scratchpad\runs\verify_rust\rawusb_list_accidental_help`.

Files are in `C:\Users\Dom\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-Dom-GitHub-freemocap-skellycam\96d4d83a-4013-4e95-a9bd-1cfedc6522c8\scratchpad`:
- Re-run results: `runs\verify_rust\` (single_*, cap_all4, mf_*, list, libusb_list, rawusb_list, cfgdesc_ab.json)
- Analysis and test scripts: `verify_tools\` (an.py, jpeghdr.py, cfgdesc_ab.py, seq_single.sh, seq_mf.sh)
